Marshalling, established by a live probe: ICWResults.GetReactionForcesAndMomentsWithSelections(step, Nothing, swsForceUnit_e, SelectedObjects, ByRef VT_VARIANT out, ByRef VT_VARIANT out, ByRef I4 err) returns the array of 16 doubles in the first ByRef VARIANT - eight values for the selected entities and eight for the entire model, each {Fx, Fy, Fz, Fres, Mx, My, Mz, Mres}. The add-in also returns the whole per-node reaction array as the method's return value; the tool never reads it. Passing Nothing for SelectedObjects is accepted, and passing a VARIANT array of one IDispatch (the restrained face) makes the selected half report that face's reaction instead of zeros; the second ByRef VARIANT then carries eight values per selected object, which the tool exposes as per_face.

The obsolete ICWResults.GetReactionForcesAndMoments(step, Nothing, units, ByRef err) still works and returns the model-wide per-node array (21087 nodes = 189783 values on the solved beam, summing to the same 2000 N); the modern method was chosen because it aggregates the model and accepts a selection.

The moment half is the sum of nodal moment reactions, which is always zero for a solid mesh because solid nodes carry no rotational degree of freedom: measured 0.0 for the axial, the transverse and the torsional cases, while the same torsional study reported 15.96 MPa and 0.10 mm. The physical moment reaction therefore lives in the force distribution and must be verified through the force components; the tool description says so.

requested_behavior: Fast and detailed traversal modes for large assemblies
evidence: list_components now takes mode='fast'|'detailed' (default detailed, so existing callers and their transforms/suppression keep working) and inspect_document exposes the same choice as component_mode. Fast mode reads only Name2 and GetPathName per instance and descends solely into components whose referenced document ends with .SLDASM; a known .SLDPRT instance is a leaf and receives no further calls at all. An unresolved or empty path counts as unknown and is still descended into, so a virtual sub-assembly cannot be missed.

Measured live 24 September 2026 on the GrabCAD assembly 'Stopnice v prostoru - Z ograjo' (77 instances: 11 top-level, 66 nested up to level 3), same session: list_components(depth=1, fast) 0.17 s / 11 instances; list_components(depth=32, fast) 36.20 s / 77 instances; list_components(depth=32, detailed) 137.05 s / 77 instances, so the full tree is 3.8x faster and the fast tree still contains every instance with complete coverage. inspect_document(sections=summary,assembly,dependencies, depth=32, component_mode='fast') took 51.14 s for the same 77 instances. The remaining cost is the two unavoidable member reads per nested instance plus GetChildren on the sub-assemblies, not the data itself.

Live test LiveComponentModeTests.test_fast_and_detailed_find_the_same_profile_instances builds a saved assembly from real DIN IPE weldment members (a 600 mm beam plus a sub-assembly holding two 300 mm beams) and asserts that fast and detailed report the same instance paths and a complete coverage, that the sub-assembly is recognised from its .sldasm path with both nested leaves found, that fast items carry no transform, configuration or suppression_state, and that detailed mode still returns a 16-element transform and a suppression state for every instance.

10 focused unit tests in solidworks_mcp/tests/test_component_traversal_modes.py count the COM member accesses on fakes and prove a leaf part is asked only for Name2 and GetPathName in fast mode while detailed mode reads all eight members.

requested_behavior: Join two bodies with a Tab and Slot feature, on flat sheets and on profiles
evidence: SW 2025 rev 33.1.1 LiveTabAndSlotTests.test_tab_is_grown_and_slot_is_cut: two 1 mm sheet-metal plate bodies built from base flanges meet at a corner, with body A edge at Y=0, Z=0 lying in the middle of body B face at Y=0. create_tab_and_slot with tab_length_mm=10, tab_height_mm=6 and slot_clearance_mm=0.2 created one persistent TabAndSlotFeature and renamed the bodies to Tab and Slot-Tab1 and Tab and Slot-Slot1. The tab body gained 60.0 mm3 (10 x 1 x 6, exactly the requested tab) and two faces; the slot body lost 12.48 mm3 ((10 + 2 x 0.2) x (1 + 2 x 0.2) x 1 mm, exactly the requested slot) and gained four faces. The body count did not change and no other body moved. GetBodies2 does not promise a stable order across documents, so the proof compares the two bodies by rank and the tool derives the tab and slot body roles from the names the feature itself assigns, falling back to the closest volume.

SW 2025 rev 33.1.1 LiveTabAndSlotProfileTests on real weldment library profiles: a Custom 50x50 through tube (2 mm walls, so its top wall spans Z 23..25) and a Custom 30X30 butting tube standing on that top face. The butting tube base rim edge lies in the through tube top face plane and its end face (the annulus) is coplanar with that plane. With tab_height_mm set to the wall thickness (2 mm, read from the geometry as the gap from the slot face down to the nearest parallel plane of the same body) and tab_thickness_mm set to the wall, the feature created one tab of exactly 10 x 2 x 2 = 40.0 mm3 whose bounding box ran from Z=25 down to Z=23 - through the wall and flush with its inner face, the up-to-the-other-face behaviour the user asked for - and cut 45.52 mm3 from the through tube. A shorter tab (half the wall) stopped inside the wall at Z=24 and left the slot with one extra face, a blind pocket bottom (19 instead of 18 faces); a longer tab (wall + 3 mm) reached Z=20 into the tube hollow section with exactly 10 x 5 x 2 = 100.0 mm3 added.

The tab reference face is now derived automatically: among the faces sharing the tab edge, the one whose normal is parallel to the slot face normal is used. On the flat plates that is the thin rim face coplanar with the target plate (60 mm3 tab) and on the tubes the end face rather than the tube wall. Setting TabFace to a perpendicular face, or leaving it unset on a tube, created no feature in every probe, which is why the rule exists.

LiveTabAndSlotTests.test_evenly_spaced_instances_and_fillet_treatment: spacing=equal with instances=3 grew three tabs (+180.0 mm3, three times 60) and cut three slots (-37.44 mm3, three times 12.48); a second call on a fresh fixture with edge_treatment=fillet and edge_treatment_mm=2 created a persistent feature whose filleted tab gained between 55 and 60 mm3 while the slot body still lost material.

LiveTabAndSlotTests.test_an_edge_outside_the_slot_plane_creates_nothing: an edge of body A one hundred millimetres away from the slot face plane produced no feature and left both body volumes untouched. LiveTabAndSlotTests.test_tool_rejects_a_single_body_part rejects a one-body part with a clear message, and the tool also refuses a tab edge and slot face that belong to the same body.

9 mock-COM unit tests in solidworks_mcp/tests/test_tab_and_slot.py verify the exact CreateDefinition(swFmTabAndSlot = 88) call, the SelectionTabEdge and SelectionSlotFace objects, the automatic TabFace pick (including perpendicular-only, curved-then-coplanar and no-neighbour cases), TabLength, SlotClearance, TabHeightType, TabHeightValue, TabEdgesType, SpacingType and SpacingNumberOfInstances in metres and enum values, the single/equal/length spacing modes, the fillet/chamfer/offset-from-edge mappings, that TabThickness stays unset unless asked for, 15 validation paths, the not-enough-bodies and non-planar-face rejections, an order-independent body-role proof, that a missing, wrong-typed, unpersisted or non-changing feature is not success, and a failing definition readback that still reports success.
